def-b-spline-space-and-basis:
## Definition

Let $p\in\mathbb N_0$, $n\ge p+1$, and $a<b$. A clamped knot vector is a nondecreasing finite sequence
$$\xi_1=\cdots=\xi_{p+1}=a<\xi_{p+2}\le\cdots\le\xi_n<\xi_{n+1}=\cdots=\xi_{n+p+1}=b,$$
with $\xi_j<\xi_{j+p+1}$ for every $1\le j\le n$. Empty interior ranges are omitted. The multiplicity $\mu(\eta)$ of an interior knot $\eta$ is its number of occurrences among $\xi_{p+2},\ldots,\xi_n$.

Write $\mathcal P_p$ for the real polynomials of degree at most $p$. The degree-$p$ spline space $S_{p,\xi}$ consists of functions that restrict to a member of $\mathcal P_p$ on each nonempty knot interval and whose derivatives through order $p-\mu(\eta)$ agree across each interior knot $\eta$. The convention $C^{-1}$ means that no matching condition is imposed. For this piecewise definition, take knot cells left-closed and right-open; at a knot with no matching condition, the value is the one from the cell on its right, and at $b$ use the left limit. Thus the function value at a discontinuous knot is specified.

The degree-zero B-spline is $B_{j,0,\xi}=\mathbf 1_{[\xi_j,\xi_{j+1})}$. For $p\ge1$, define recursively
$$B_{j,p,\xi}(x)=\frac{x-\xi_j}{\xi_{j+p}-\xi_j}B_{j,p-1,\xi}(x)+\frac{\xi_{j+p+1}-x}{\xi_{j+p+1}-\xi_{j+1}}B_{j+1,p-1,\xi}(x),$$
where a term with zero denominator is defined to be zero. At $b$, set $B_{j,p,\xi}(b)$ equal to its left limit. The basis and regularity properties of this recursively defined family are proved in [[thm-spline-polynomial-reproduction]].
def-natural-cubic-spline:
## Definition

Let $[a,b]$ be a bounded interval and let $a\le t_1<\cdots<t_r\le b$ with $r\ge2$. A natural cubic spline with knots $t_1,\ldots,t_r$ is a $C^2$ function on $[a,b]$ that is a polynomial of degree at most three on every $[t_j,t_{j+1}]$, has second derivative zero at $t_1$ and $t_r$, and is extended linearly on $[a,t_1]$ and $[t_r,b]$ when those intervals are nonempty. The knots $t_j$ are the distinct breakpoints; repeated observations at the same input do not create additional knots.
def-local-spline-quasi-interpolant:
## Definition

Fix a degree-$p$ spline space $S_{p,\xi}$ on $[a,b]$, an exponent $1\le q\le\infty$, and an integer $0\le l\le p$. A **local quasi-interpolant** is a linear map $Q$ from continuous $L^q$ functions on $[a,b]$ into $S_{p,\xi}$ with the following properties. For every nonempty knot interval $I_m$, there is a neighborhood $J_m\subseteq[a,b]$ that is a union of at most $M$ adjacent knot intervals such that (i) if $f=g$ almost everywhere on $J_m$, then $Qf=Qg$ almost everywhere on $I_m$; (ii) $Qv=v$ for every $v\in\mathcal P_l$; and (iii) for a constant $C_Q$ independent of the mesh, $\|Qf\|_{L^q(I_m)}\le C_Q\|f\|_{L^q(J_m)}$. Here $M$ bounds both the number of intervals in each $J_m$ and the number of neighborhoods $J_m$ containing any one point. The derivative and continuous-representative conventions for Sobolev inputs are those of [[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]] and [[cor-one-dimensional-w-one-p-functions-have-absolutely-continuous-representatives]].

The coefficient-functional formulation in Lyche–Manni–Speleers is one sufficient way to obtain these local stability and reproduction properties. The definition here records the operator hypotheses used in the approximation proof.
def-natural-cubic-smoothing-spline:
## Definition

Assume AC. Let $[a,b]$ be a bounded interval, let $(x_i,y_i)_{i=1}^n\in([a,b]\times\mathbb R)^n$, assume at least two distinct input values, and let $\lambda>0$. For $g\in W^{2,2}(a,b)$ use its unique continuous representative on $[a,b]$ supplied by the one-dimensional Sobolev representative theorem. The natural cubic smoothing spline is the unique minimizer, whose existence and uniqueness are proved in [[thm-natural-cubic-smoothing-spline-exists-uniquely]], of
$$J(g)=\sum_{i=1}^n(y_i-g(x_i))^2+\lambda\int_a^b|D^2g(t)|^2\,dt.$$

The requirement of two distinct inputs is essential. The penalty is the squared $L^2$ norm of the second weak derivative; the data term uses the distinct-input interpolation convention in [[def-natural-cubic-spline]].
thm-natural-cubic-interpolant-exists-uni:
## Statement

Let $r\ge2$, $a\le x_1<\cdots<x_r\le b$, and $y_1,\ldots,y_r\in\mathbb R$. There is exactly one natural cubic spline $s$ on $[a,b]$ with $s(x_i)=y_i$ for each $i$. On each interval $[x_i,x_{i+1}]$ it is the cubic with endpoint values $y_i,y_{i+1}$ and endpoint second derivatives $M_i,M_{i+1}$, where $M_1=M_r=0$ and the interior values solve the positive-definite tridiagonal system
$$h_{i-1}M_{i-1}+2(h_{i-1}+h_i)M_i+h_iM_{i+1}=6\left(\frac{y_{i+1}-y_i}{h_i}-\frac{y_i-y_{i-1}}{h_{i-1}}\right),\quad 2\le i\le r-1,$$
with $h_i=x_{i+1}-x_i>0$. The interpolant is linear outside $[x_1,x_r]$.
thm-spline-polynomial-reproduction:
## Statement

Let $p\in\mathbb N_0$ and let $\xi$ be a clamped knot vector as in [[def-b-spline-space-and-basis]]. The recursively defined degree-$p$ B-splines are nonnegative, are supported on $[\xi_j,\xi_{j+p+1}]$, and are piecewise polynomials of degree at most $p$. At a knot of multiplicity $\mu\le p$, each B-spline is $C^{p-\mu}$; multiplicity $p+1$ imposes no continuity requirement. On every nonempty knot interval $[\xi_m,\xi_{m+1})$, the active functions $B_{m-p,p,\xi},\ldots,B_{m,p,\xi}$ form a basis of $\mathcal P_p$ and sum to one. Globally, the $n$ B-splines form a basis of $S_{p,\xi}$. In particular, every $q\in\mathcal P_p$ has a unique expansion $q=\sum_{j=1}^n c_jB_{j,p,\xi}$ on $[a,b]$.
def-series-spline-least-squares:
## Definition

Let $p_K(x)=(B_{1,p,\xi}(x),\ldots,B_{K,p,\xi}(x))^T$ be a specified degree-$p$ B-spline basis on the data domain, and let $(X_i,Y_i)_{i=1}^n$ be observed real-valued data. Form the design matrix $P\in\mathbb R^{n\times K}$ with row $p_K(X_i)^T$. The **series least-squares fitted training vector** is
$$\widehat{\mathbf g}_K=\Pi_{\operatorname{col}(P)}\mathbf Y,$$
the orthogonal projection of $\mathbf Y=(Y_1,\ldots,Y_n)^T$ onto the column space of $P$. Conditional on the realized design, this is the fixed-design least-squares fitted vector of [[def-fixed-design-projection-estimator]]. Equivalently, it is $P\widehat\beta$ for any minimizer $\widehat\beta$ of $\|\mathbf Y-P\beta\|_2^2$; all such minimizers have the same fitted training vector. The training prediction loss relative to a specified target vector $\mathbf g_0=(g_0(X_1),\ldots,g_0(X_n))^T$ is $n^{-1}\|\widehat{\mathbf g}_K-\mathbf g_0\|_2^2$. This definition specifies training fitted values and makes no test-risk assertion.
thm-natural-cubic-smoothing-spline-exist:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $[a,b]$, $\lambda>0$, and data $(x_i,y_i)_{i=1}^n$ satisfy the hypotheses of [[def-natural-cubic-smoothing-spline]], with $r\ge2$ distinct inputs $t_1<\cdots<t_r$. Then $J$ has a unique minimizer over $W^{2,2}(a,b)$. It is the natural cubic spline with knots at $t_1,\ldots,t_r$, extended linearly to $a$ and $b$ where needed.
thm-sobolev-spline-quasi-interpolant-rat:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $p\ge0$, $0\le l\le p$, $1\le q\le\infty$, and let $Q$ be a bounded local quasi-interpolant as in [[def-local-spline-quasi-interpolant]] on a knot mesh in $[a,b]$. Let $f\in W^{l+1,q}(a,b)$ and use its continuous Sobolev representative. For each nonempty mesh cell $I_m$, let $J_m$ be the corresponding neighborhood, let $h_m$ be the largest cell length in $J_m$, and suppose $|J_m|\le M h_m$ with overlap multiplicity at most $M$. Then
$$\|f-Qf\|_{L^q(I_m)}\le (1+C_Q)\frac{M^{l+1}}{l!}h_m^{l+1}\|D^{l+1}f\|_{L^q(J_m)}.$$
Writing $h=\max_m h_m$, the global bound is
$$\|f-Qf\|_{L^q([a,b])}\le (1+C_Q)\frac{M^{l+1+1/q}}{l!}h^{l+1}\|D^{l+1}f\|_{L^q([a,b])},$$
where $1/q=0$ for $q=\infty$. In particular, on a uniform mesh with interior knots of multiplicity $p+1$, the cellwise $L^2$ projector onto $\mathcal P_p$ is a local quasi-interpolant and gives the order-$h^s$ approximation bound for every integer $1\le s\le p+1$.
thm-series-training-risk:
## Statement

Let $n,K\ge1$, let $X_i\in[a,b]$ and $Y_i\in\mathbb R$ be iid pairs, and suppose the one-observation law is $P_X(dx)\kappa(x,dy)$ for a supplied Borel probability kernel $\kappa$ from $([a,b],\mathcal B([a,b]))$ to $(\mathbb R,\mathcal B(\mathbb R))$. Assume a Borel function $g_0:[a,b]\to\mathbb R$ is supplied such that, for $P_X$-almost every $x$, $\int |y|\,\kappa(x,dy)<\infty$, $g_0(x)=\int y\,\kappa(x,dy)$, and $\int (y-g_0(x))^2\,\kappa(x,dy)\le\Delta$ for a finite $\Delta\ge0$. Let $p_K:[a,b]\to\mathbb R^K$ be a fixed Borel $K$-dimensional spline basis and assume a deterministic $\bar\beta_K\in\mathbb R^K$ and constants $C,\gamma>0$ satisfy
$$E\{g_0(X)-p_K(X)^T\bar\beta_K\}^2\le C^2K^{-2\gamma}.$$
Then, with the fitted training vector $\widehat{\mathbf g}_K$ from [[def-series-spline-least-squares]] and $\mathbf g_0=(g_0(X_1),\ldots,g_0(X_n))^T$,
$$E\left[\frac1n\|\widehat{\mathbf g}_K-\mathbf g_0\|_2^2\right]\le\frac{\Delta K}{n}+C^2K^{-2\gamma}.$$
This is expected empirical training-design loss.
cor-series-spline-sobolev-training-risk-:
## Statement

Assume AC. Let $X,Y$ be real random variables with $E|Y|<\infty$, choose a regular conditional law $Q(x,dy)$ of $Y$ given $X=x$, and let $g_0$ be the selected Borel regression-function version from [[def-regression-target-version]]. Suppose $P_X$ is supported on $[a,b]$ with density bounded by $M_X$, $g_0\in W^{s,2}(a,b)$ for an integer $s\ge1$, and $\int (y-g_0(x))^2Q(x,dy)\le\Delta$ for $P_X$-almost every $x$. For degree $p\ge s-1$, use a uniform partition into $J$ cells and the B-spline space with each interior knot repeated $p+1$ times, so its dimension is $K=(p+1)J$. For iid observations from this joint law, let $\widehat{\mathbf g}_K$ be the fitted training vector and $\mathbf g_0=(g_0(X_1),\ldots,g_0(X_n))^T$. Then
$$E\left[\frac1n\|\widehat{\mathbf g}_K-\mathbf g_0\|_2^2\right]\le\frac{\Delta K}{n}+C_{s,p,M_X,a,b}\,K^{-2s}\|D^sg_0\|_{L^2(a,b)}^2.$$
Choosing $J\asymp n^{1/(2s+1)}$ (equivalently $K\asymp n^{1/(2s+1)}$ for fixed $p$) gives expected empirical training risk $O(n^{-2s/(2s+1)})$. This is not an independent-test-risk bound.
